title: In on a Secret? — That's Dramatic Irony
skills: identify situations in which the audience knows more than a character
analyze how dramatic irony creates tension, humor, or suspense
explain how irony contributes to meaning and audience response
alignment_note: Introduces dramatic irony as a literary device in which the audience knows information that one or more characters do not. Supports close reading, analysis of suspense and humor, interpretation of audience perspective, and understanding of author's craft across high school English courses.
